title: LIHEAP AVAILABLE
full_story:
CEFS Economic Opportunity Corporation’s Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) still has funding available.  Applications for the current program year will be accepted through August 14th.

Households that applied on or after October 1st, may only reapply if facing utility disconnection.  Those who previously received reconnection assistance should contact their local CEFS Outreach Office to check eligibility for additional help.

Since October 1st, CEFS has approved $537,216.00 in energy benefits for 716 Clay County households, averaging $750 per household.  An additional 229 households received $168,613 in emergency reconnection assistance, averaging $736.

Monthly Income Eligibility are as follows: 1 person can make up to $3,332 per month, 2 people can make up to $4,357 a month, 3 people can make up to $5,382, and 4 people can make up to $6,407 per month.  Income limits for larger households are available at www.cefseoc.org or www.liheapillinois.com.

To schedule an appointment, contact the CEFS Clay County Outreach Office at 618-662-4024 which is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am – 4:30 pm, or schedule online at www.cefseoc.org.  Applications can be completed in person or by phone, and documents may be submitted in person, by mail, or electronically.  Those needing any special accommodation should contact their local CEFS office.

LIHEAP is funded by the US Department of Health and Human Services and the Illinois Department of Commerce & Economic Opportunity.  CEFS administers the program in Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie, and Shelby counties.

title: APRIL UNEMPLOYMENT
full_story:
The Clay County unemployment rate for April was 4%, down from 5.2% in March and .2% higher than the same month, one year ago.  The numbers translate into 5,736 in the labor force, 159 less than March.  There were 229 unemployed, 80 less than last month.

All area counties had lower unemployment rates in April from March.  Effingham County had the lowest rate in the are at 3.3% down from 4.5% in March.  Followed by Jasper County at 3.4% down from 4.2% last month.  The lowest unemployment rate in the state is in Monroe County at 2.6% and the highest in the state is again in Edwards County where the April rate was 11%, down 3.9% from the previous month.

The Illinois Department of Employment Security reported that total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 175 jobs in April 2026.  Employment gains were posted by employers in the Construction, Manufacturing, Government, Trade-Transportation-Utilities, and Professional-Business Services sectors.  Payroll losses were seen in the Private Education-Health Services, Financial Activities, Information, and Other Services sectors.

The state unemployment rate for April was 4.7% down from 5.2% the previous month and up from 4.2% a year ago.  The US unemployment rate for April was 4%, down from 4.3% the previous month and up from 3.9% in April of last year.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
The American Red Cross is asking you to donate blood as we head toward the summer months.  The organization says there is traditionally more of a need at this time of year and all blood types are needed, especially Type O, which can be used when a patient’s blood type is unknown.

There is a blood drive today, from 1 to 6 pm at the Clay Electric Coop.  Then there will be two Blood Drives next week.  The first is at the Blue Point Free Will Baptist Church on Tuesday, June 9th from Noon to 6 pm and then on Thursday, June 11th from Noon to 5 pm at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.  Donors at these drives will receive a $15 gift card by email.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).

title: BUDGET PASSES
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer issued the following statement after Democrat lawmakers passed a $56 billion budget that includes over $800 million in new taxes, fees, and revenue enhancements:

“Eight years under Governor Pritzker have given Illinois families a bigger government, higher costs, and fewer reasons to stay.

“This is Pritzker’s eighth budget, and to the shock of no one, his record has not changed.  Spending is up more than 40%, which is more than $16 billion in new spending.  Illinois families are buried under the highest tax burden in the nation, and taxpayers are once again being asked to pay more for the same failed results.

“Meanwhile, Illinois continues to fall behind.  We have one of the highest unemployment rates in the nation, our economic growth is significantly lagging behind our neighbors, and census numbers prove families and businesses are fleeing the state in droves because they cannot afford the cost of doing business or raising a family in Illinois.

“Yet, here we are again.  This budget was negotiated behind closed doors and dropped in the final hours of session, leaving legislators and the public no time to review it.  That is not transparency.  That is not good government.  That is Springfield Democrats, led by J.B. Pritzker, hiding the details until the last possible moment and hoping taxpayers do not notice the cost.

“After eight years of bleeding taxpayers, Governor Pritzker wants to call this progress.  It is not.  But Illinois families know better.  They are cutting back, making sacrifices, and wondering why state government never seems to do the same.

“This budget is not relief.  It is Pritzker’s bill for eight years of continued failure.”

State Representative Blaine Wilhour of Beecher City voted against the revenue bill and spoke against it during debate on the floor, telling his Democrat colleagues there is never enough money for their tax and spend ways.

title: CHAMBER GOLF SCRAMBLE

Check-in will begin at 11:30 am inside the Clubhouse, lunch is at Noon, and tee-time at 1:00pm on the day of the tournament.

title: LAST STREET MACHINE NATIONALS
full_story:
After 40 years, Street Machine Nationals announced its final event in Du Quoin.

In a Facebook post, they said that June 5th through 7th will be their final car show in Du Quoin.  The event will take place at the Du Quoin State Fairgrounds.

“This is truly the end of an era,” said Matt Hickman, managing director of Bonnier LLC Motorsports & Outdoor Group.  “Street Machine Nationals in Du Quoin has meant so much to so many people over the years, participants, exhibitors, sponsors, staff, and fans alike.  While we are looking toward the future of the brand, we also wanted to make sure we properly honor the history and community that made this event special for 40 years.”

Organizers say attendees can expect special anniversary moments throughout the weekend, including commemorative merchandise, collectibles, legacy displays and tributes celebrating the event’s long-standing history in Du Quoin.

title: FTC LAUNCHES INVESTIGATION
full_story:
The Federal Trade Commission launched an antitrust investigation into the concentrated fertilizer industry and its pricing power, FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson announced Thursday.

“USDA has shown the single largest increase in input costs for farmers across the United States since 2020 has come from fertilizer,” Ferguson said to commodity group representatives from 18 states during an event held by the Texas Corn Producers in Texas, Politico reported.

“These continued price increases are not something our nation, much less our farmers, can continue to ignore,” Ferguson said.

FTC’s move marks the first formal federal investigation with subpoena power and the potential for antitrust enforcement if wrongdoing is uncovered.

Ferguson said the high prices “do not always mean” illegal activity, but the FTC “cannot rule out” the possibility of anti-competitive action in the fertilizer industry.

The Justice Department previously initiated a separate probe into potential anti-competitive practices of fertilizer companies.  The Trump administration has also touted a September 2025 memorandum of understanding between the Agriculture Department and Justice Department “formalizing” the partnership to protect competition in agricultural inputs including fertilizer.
